storyboardBeats.narration: Your brake fluid is quietly pulling water out of the air. That's not a defect. That's chemistry.
storyboardBeats.providerScene: Extreme macro, brake fluid reservoir cap slowly unscrewed, pale amber fluid visible inside, single shaft of light catching the surface, shallow depth of field, slow push-in, moody garage-bay lighting, cinematic automotive commercial look, 9:16 vertical framing

storyboardBeats.narration: Brake fluid is hygroscopic — it absorbs moisture through the lines over time, even sealed.
storyboardBeats.providerScene: Macro shot of a test strip dipping into a small sample cup of brake fluid, pads on the strip beginning to shift color, soft overhead key light, shallow DOF, static hold then slow tilt, 9:16 vertical framing

storyboardBeats.narration: More water in the fluid means a lower boiling point — and a spongier pedal exactly when you need it firm.
storyboardBeats.providerScene: Close-up comparison of two test strips side by side on a clean workbench, one pale/clean-reading, one visibly shifted toward the high-moisture color band, even top-down light, slow lateral dolly, 9:16 vertical framing

storyboardBeats.narration: It's also how corrosion starts inside steel brake lines, from the inside out, where you can't see it.
storyboardBeats.providerScene: Macro shot of a brake line fitting on a workbench, rack-focus from a clean fitting to a second fitting with light surface corrosion, dim garage lighting shifting cooler, slow rack focus pull, texture-forward, 9:16 vertical framing
